answer: The [[Top Bar]] at the top of the editor shows page navigation, commands and connection status. If a sync takes longer than a second, a black circle progress indicator also appears there.

--- Sync.md ---
Sync | Status
If sync takes longer than a second, a black circle progress indicator will appear in the [[Top Bar]].

--- Top Bar.md ---
Top Bar | description
Page navigation, commands and connection status at the top of the editor.

--- Guide/Git Sync.md ---
Syncing with a remote | Syncing with a remote > Progress and timing
The connection overview shows live status and the last successful sync. Members can use **Git: View status** and **Git: Review conflicts**. Writers can request **Git: Sync now**. Space History also shows Git sync status. Unknown or unavailable status is not the same as being up to date.

Local changes are pushed after an automatic commit. The revisions **Commit frequency** setting controls that timing. **Check remote changes** controls how often SilverBullet checks for other people’s commits. **Only when this space changes** disables periodic remote checks, but a sync triggered by your changes still fetches and merges before pushing. It is not a push-only mode.

Pulled changes reach open editors through the normal file-change mechanism. Network failures show an error and retry with backoff. Authentication or configuration problems require repairing the connection.

--- Workbench/Overview.md ---
Overview
* **Edits by person:** who made the edits of the last month, with a count for each. It only shows when more than one person edits the space.
* **Git sync:** the state of Git sync, when it is enabled: “Sync failed”, “Paused”, “Syncing…” or the number of conflicted files when sync isn’t idle, otherwise the number of pending changes or “Up to date”.
* **Runtime:** the SilverBullet version, and how many scripts and styles are loaded. Scripts and styles link to their tabs.

--- Troubleshooting.md ---
Desktop | Server
If the Server cannot be reached, check that its process is running, then inspect its logs and any reverse-proxy logs. See [[Log]]. Verify the listening address and port in [[Install/Configuration]] and the setup in [[Install/Network and Internet]]. If the Server responds but access is denied, check the account and space access settings in the [[Dashboard]].

For errors after the editor opens, inspect [[Workbench/Console]] and the browser’s JavaScript console. The following browser options help isolate scripts, styles, plugs and offline-cache problems.
